title: Advanced RxJS Operators for HTTP 🚀
description: Use switchMap, mergeMap, forkJoin, and debounceTime for common real‑world patterns.

slides.title: Beyond Simple GET 🔗
slides.content:
# Chaining HTTP Requests

Often one request depends on another. You can chain them using **higher‑order mapping operators**:

* `switchMap` – cancel previous inner observable when new outer emission arrives. Perfect for search.
* `mergeMap` – run all inner observables concurrently. Good for multiple independent requests.
* `concatMap` – run inner observables in order, one after another.
* `exhaustMap` – ignore new outer emissions while inner is active (e.g., login).

quizData.question: Which operator cancels a previous inner observable when a new outer value arrives?
quizData.explanation: `switchMap` unsubscribes from the previous inner observable and switches to the new one.

slides.title: debounceTime & distinctUntilChanged ⏲️
slides.content:
When building a search input, use `debounceTime` to wait until the user stops typing, and `distinctUntilChanged` to avoid duplicate requests.

```typescript
this.searchTerms.pipe(
  debounceTime(300),
  distinctUntilChanged(),
  switchMap(term => this.searchService.search(term))
);
```
This drastically reduces server load.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Choose the Right Map Operator

* Search? `switchMap`.
* Multiple independent fetches? `mergeMap`.
* Order matters? `concatMap`.
* Prevent double submit? `exhaustMap`.

quizData.question: `forkJoin` will emit only after all input Observables have completed.
quizData.explanation: `forkJoin` waits for all observables to complete, then emits the last values as an array.
